questions.question: If you need to back your vehicle into an alley, what should you do first?

options.text: Drive directly into the alley parking space.
Turn right to position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Drive past the alley and stop at a right angle to the outer edge.
Drive past the alley and stop parallel to the outer edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive past the alley and stop parallel to the outer edge.
questions.explanation: To back into an alley, first drive past it and stop your vehicle parallel to the outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking space. Your vehicle should be parked straight between the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: A person watching a tank being loaded or unloaded must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
Know the dangers of the materials being handled.

questions.explanation: The supervisor watching a hazardous materials tank must be alert, watch the tank at all times, stay within 25 feet, know the material dangers, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed. A chemical suit is not required.

questions.question: When driving on an expressway during your skills test, you should:

options.text: Use your mirrors to check traffic regularly.
Drive on the left side of your lane.
Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to check traffic regularly.
questions.explanation: On an expressway during the driving test, keep proper lane position, maintain safe distance from other vehicles, and drive at the posted speed. Always check your mirrors and look around for traffic in all directions.

questions.question: When approaching a curve during the driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Check traffic thoroughly in all directions.
Slow down before entering the curve.
Keep your vehicle in its lane.
Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.
questions.explanation: When approaching a curve, check traffic in all directions, slow down before entering the curve so you don't need to brake during it, and stay in your lane. Avoid using the brakes while turning.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, the landing gear should be:

options.text: More worn on one side than the other.

questions.explanation: Check that the landing gear has no missing parts and is fully raised. The crank handle must be secure, and the support frame must not be damaged.

questions.question: When transporting Division 1.1 materials, the floor liner must be made from:
questions.explanation: Use a floor liner for Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials. The floor must be tight, and the liner must be non-metallic or non-ferrous metal (metals without iron or iron alloys).

questions.question: During the driving skills test, you will be evaluated on how you use gears. You should not:

options.text: Choose a gear that makes the engine rev too much.
Shift while driving through an intersection.

questions.explanation: Use gears that keep the engine from revving or slowing too much. Avoid grinding or clashing gears. Do not shift while turning or going through intersections.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Point to or touch each item you check.
Explain what you are checking and why.

questions.explanation: During the inspection test, walk around the vehicle and point to or touch each part while explaining what you are checking and why. You do not need to crawl under the vehicle or look under the hood.

questions.question: What tool should you use to check if tires are properly inflated?
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure during the vehicle inspection test. Simply kicking the tires is not acceptable and will not earn passing credit.

questions.question: No one should smoke within ____ of a vehicle carrying Class 3 or Division 2.1 hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a placarded tank carrying Class 3 or Division 2.1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, where should you NOT park the vehicle?

options.text: For only short periods of time

questions.explanation: Do not park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Also do not park within 5 feet of the road. Park only for brief periods when needed to operate the vehicle.

questions.question: When accepting a hazardous materials package, what should you check?

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on the packages
The shipping paper is written in code
All packages are labeled as poison

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on the packages
questions.explanation: Compare the shipping papers to the markings and labels on the packages when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, what should you do with the engine?
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids. The only exception is if the engine must run to operate a pump.

questions.question: What should you check about tire wear during a vehicle inspection?

options.text: The insides are more worn than the outsides
The outsides are more worn than the insides
The middle is more worn than the outsides

questions.explanation: Check that tire treads are worn evenly during your vehicle inspection.

questions.question: What should you do when crossing railroad tracks?
questions.explanation: When crossing railroad tracks, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is in the crossing.

questions.question: Who can transport hazardous materials?

options.text: Any driver if the materials weigh under 50 pounds
Any driver in a rural area
A driver with a CDL and HazMat endorsement

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver with a CDL and HazMat endorsement
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle used to transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: What is used to warn people about hazardous materials on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped warning signs called placards are placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials to warn people.

questions.question: What is important to know about transporting radioactive materials?

options.text: Radiation passes through to other packages
The packages must be carried in the cab
The packages must be loaded on their side

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation passes through to other packages
questions.explanation: Radiation surrounds radioactive packages and passes through to nearby packages. Because of this, there are limits on how many radioactive packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control test, what counts as a look?

options.text: Walking to the back of the vehicle to check its position
Using side mirrors to check the vehicle's position
Looking out of the driver's window to check the vehicle's position
Glancing over your shoulder to check blind spots

questions.correctAnswerText: Walking to the back of the vehicle to check its position
questions.explanation: A look is when you open your door, leave the driver's seat, and walk to the back of the vehicle to check its position. You may only do one look during the straight line backing exercise. You may do up to two looks during any other exercise.

questions.question: Which level of government controls hazardous materials laws?
questions.explanation: Federal, state, and local governments all create regulations for transporting hazardous materials because of the risks involved.

questions.question: What should a carrier do if hazardous materials are not properly prepared?

options.text: Accept the shipment, but make a notation on the paperwork

questions.explanation: A carrier must refuse shipments of hazardous materials that are not properly prepared.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives, how can you warn other drivers?

options.text: By standing on the roadway and waving your arms.
By keeping the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: When your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives, use electric lights or reflective triangles to warn other drivers. Do not use flares or open flames, as they could start a fire.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Complete the test without a moving violation.
Obey all traffic signs and signals, but only if other traffic is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey all traffic signs and signals, but only if other traffic is present.
questions.explanation: You must wear your safety belt, obey all traffic laws, signs, and signals, and avoid moving violations. You must obey traffic signs and signals at all times, regardless of whether other traffic is present.

questions.question: What is a portable tank?

options.text: Cannot be removed from a vehicle.
Is not permanently attached to a vehicle.
Is permanently attached to a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not permanently attached to a vehicle.
questions.explanation: A portable tank is not permanently attached to a vehicle. It is bulk packaging that can be removed. Cargo tanks, on the other hand, stay on a vehicle at all times.

questions.question: Which agency coordinates emergency response to chemical hazards?

options.text: The United Center for Chemical Assistance

questions.explanation: The National Response Center helps police and firefighters coordinate emergency response to chemical hazards.

questions.question: How should pre-trip inspections be done?

options.text: Differently each time, emphasizing different items.
The same way each time so you are less likely to forget something.
By someone other than the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you are less likely to forget something.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This helps you remember all the important items to check.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials should not be placed in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: Heaters are not allowed in trailers carrying Class 1 explosives, Class 2.1 flammable gases, or Class 3 flammable liquids.

questions.question: During the skills test, if you must stop before making a turn, you should:

options.text: Stop after the stop line to get a better view.
Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: Stop smoothly before the stop line. Keep your front wheels straight ahead and do not let your vehicle roll. Stop where you can still see the rear tires of the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: If a shipping paper has both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, the hazardous materials should be:

options.text: Circled by a pen or marker.
Written the same way as the non-hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Highlight hazardous materials in a contrasting color to make them stand out from non-hazardous materials on the same shipping paper.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, you must maintain ____ with the vehicle at all times.
questions.explanation: Face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact while exiting. For a bus, hold the handrail. Failing to do this may result in an automatic test failure.
